text:
maria: Heads up — saw a regression on prod after the multi-variant routing tweak. Batch sizes dropped ~30% on p50 traffic and KV cache miss rate jumped. attaching quick profiler snapshot.

derek: ugh. which change specifically? the compat set expansion or the new fallback ordering?

maria: it correlates with yesterday's change that made fallback prefer smaller, faster variants to hit latency SLOs. but that seems to be fragmenting batches. logs: `batch_formation: avg_batch=4.7 -> 3.2, batch_wait_ms=12->18` and `kv_cache_miss: 6%->21%`

elaine: can you paste the profiler flamegraph link? also which model families were in the mix?

maria: https://internal.redwood/prof/171850 — mix: rwd-medium-v1 + rwd-compat-lite + community-quant. traffic skewed ~70% medium, 20% lite, 10% quant.

sam: likely two things: (1) routing to smaller variants reduces opportunity for kernel coalescing (kernel selection warms different codepaths), (2) fallback that pins to fastest variant increases interleaving across compat sets, so batching groups are smaller and more heterogeneous.

prashant: agreed. we also saw earlier that small-variant preference increases cache churn because KV keys are variant-specific. Even if compatible, we store separate KV entries.

maria: quick reproduction in staging shows the same sawtooth batch size over 10m: `avg_batch_per_second [25, 5, 22, 6, 24]` — looks like periodic fallback oscillation.

ci-bot: deploy 1718499800 triggered routing-policy:v3 -> canary rollout 12:14 UTC yesterday.

derek: for a quick mitigation, can we change queue_policy to 'agglomerative' which tries to merge partial windows across compat sets, or bump token_budget_target from 256->384?

sam: 'agglomerative' sounds promising — it will try to merge by request age and token count rather than strict variant affinity. downside: slightly higher p99 latency if kernels mismatch.

elaine: propose an experiment: 1) staging: enable agglomerative for 2 hours on canary pool; 2) enable KV shared-keying for compatible variants (proto change) on same pool; 3) monitor batch size, kv miss, p50/p99.

maria: experiment script i used: ```json
{"route":"/gen","queue_policy":"agglomerative","token_budget_target":384,"compat_sets":[["rwd-medium-v1","rwd-compat-lite"]]}
```

prashant: small note: shared-keying requires a safe-hash of model signature — tests exist in tools/kv/shared_key_test.py. We'll need a migration plan for hot keys.

sam: also check kernel selector logs — the selector sometimes falls back from optimized-fp16 kernels to generic-int8 when batch shapes are inconsistent. that increases per-token time. pattern: `kernel_choice: optimized_fp16->generic_int8` when batch heterogeneity > 0.4

derek: OK I'm going to roll a canary with agglomerative + token_budget_target=384 on pool-canary-3 for 30m. will watch kv_miss, batch_size, kernel_choice.

maria: thanks. data to watch: `batch.avg_size`, `batch.heterogeneity`, `kv.cache_miss_pct`, `kernel.switch_rate`, `p50_latency`. if anyone has thresholds to add, ping me.

elaine: add `compat.fallback_rate` (how often we fall back to non-preferred variant) and `batch.wait_ms` to list.

ci-bot: canary started: pool-canary-3 @1718500120.

maria: initial 10m: avg_batch 3.3 -> 4.8, kv_miss 19% -> 9%, kernel.switch_rate down 2.4x. p50 latency +8ms, p99 +18ms.

prashant: promising — cache win looks real. we should validate quality/regression on a small eval set before rolling wide.

sam: if quality holds, plan: (A) enable agglomerative on dedicated pools for 24h, (B) land shared-keying opt-in behind flag, (C) follow up with kernel selector tweak to prefer 'family-matching' kernels even if batch shape slightly off.

derek: added follow-up ticket: INF-7523 (rollout plan + eval gating).

maria: cool. I'll keep collecting traces and post a short writeup with flamegraphs. thanks all :thumbsup:
